analysis: Both units are base-side excerpts of docs/reference/configuration.md. The changed ranges (head and base lines 969, 977-978, 1115, 1712-1713) fall outside the supplied excerpts (lines 486-938). The visible patch only expands the documentation of the cluster resource_policy_sha256 field (the Qwen tensor-assistant fields, line 969). That is a documentation change describing a digest composition, and I identified no change to security controls or code. I examined the base text for configuration-security content that the changed lines could interact with. The SSD prefix cache section (T-041) covers DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gating, the 1800s TTL cap, the cache.directory and volume_uuid checks, the debug-only KEK file and the ephemeral-key fallback. The pair-approval catalog (strict parsing, digest pins) and the env-scrubber list are also documented there. None of these is modified in the visible patch. The documented behavior matches the threat model: the TTL can only be shortened, the DEBUG key file is not compiled into release builds, and the test-root and ephemeral options require an explicit opt-in and are not forwarded to LaunchAgents. Remaining limits: the patch excerpt is truncated and the changed lines at 977-978, 1115 and 1712-1713 are not visible to me. The claims about the tensor-assistant resource-policy digest and the pair-serving-grant semantics cannot be checked against the code in the supplied evidence. They are documentation claims about the cluster pair catalog, which the platform owns. A later pass should confirm that the documented digest composition matches ClusterPublicTensorAssistant.resourcePolicyFields and the coordinator's NativeRuntimeCatalog. I flag no security regression.
